full_judgment: 2. The respondent here in filed the above mentioned Title Suit No. 637 of 1981 for declaration of title to the suit property and also for a further declaration that the order dated 22.03.1978 passed by the defendant No. 2 (A.D.C. Revenue) treating the suit property as vested and non-resident property is illegal, void, malafide and not binding upon the plaintiff. The case of the plaintiff, in short, is that the suit property, as described in the schedule to the plaint, together with other properties originally belonged to Shashi Mohan Saha, Surendra Chandra Saha, Khetra Mohan Saha, Raj Mohan Saha, Rajendra Chandra Saha, Suresh Chandra Saha, Ranjit Kumar Saha, Brojendra Chandra saha, Gogan Chandra Saha and Bhagaban Chandra Saha. Those owners sold the suit property along with their other ejmali lands to Bhakta Das Saha, Ananta Kumar Saha, Sachinanandan Saha and Joshoda Lal Saha by two registered Kabalas dated 05.03.1935. Thereafter, Sachinanandan Saha and Joshoda Lal Saha surrendered their interest in the suit property along with other lands in favour of Bhakta Das Saha and Ananta Kumar Saha by a registered deed dated 26.07.1938. On the basis of Partition Suit No. 29 of 1938, the suit property together with other lands fell in the saham of Bhakta Das Saha alone. Bhakta Das Saha died leaving 5 sons, namely, Haripada Das Saha, Shaoni Manda Das Saha, Durga Sankar Das Saha, Gouri Sarkar Das Saha and Jogesh Chandra Saha, Subsequently there was an amicable partition of their paternal properties amongst 5 brothers and the suit property fell in the exclusive share of Haripada Das Saha along with some other properties. Thus Haripada Das Saha became owner and possessor of the disputed property and he got his name recorded in the S.A. Khatian vide order dated 02.01.1973 passed in Mutation Case No. 37/N of 1972-73. Municipal holding was also opened in his name and he had been possessing the suit property on payment of regular rents to the Government and also paid taxes to the Narayangonj Municipality. During R.S. operation, his name was also recorded and he was possessing the suit property by letting out the same to different monthly tenants. Thereafter, Haripada Das Saha transferred the suit property to the plaintiff by a registered Kabala dated 03.01.1976 for valuable consideration and delivered possession in her favour. Brother of the vendor, Namely, Durga Sankar Saha was also an attesting witness to the said transfer deed and thereby admitted exclusive ownership of Haripada Das Saha in the suit property so transferred. He also admitted exclusive ownership of his brother Haripada Das Saha by swearing affidavit before the Magistrate, 1st Class, Dhaka. After purchase of the suit property, the plaintiff got her name mutated in place of her vendor Haripada Das Saha on 12.01.1976 and she has been paying rents to the Government regularly. Her name was also recorded against the municipal holding of the suit property and she has been paying taxes. She has been possessing the suit property by letting out the same to different monthly tenants as before.
